cec.name: Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC)
cec.definition: The total capacity of a soil to hold exchangeable cations (Ca2+, Mg2+, K+, Na+, NH4+).
cec.significance: Higher CEC soils (clays and high organic matter soils) hold nutrients longer and resist leaching compared to low CEC sandy soils.

soil_texture.name: Soil Texture & Structure
soil_texture.definition: The relative proportion of sand (0.05-2.0 mm), silt (0.002-0.05 mm), and clay (<0.002 mm) particles.
soil_texture.significance: Determines soil aeration, water-holding capacity, infiltration rate, root penetration resistance, and tillage ease.

organic_matter.name: Soil Organic Matter (SOM)
organic_matter.definition: The fraction of the soil that consists of plant or animal tissue in various stages of decomposition.
organic_matter.significance: Enhances microbial biodiversity, improves soil water retention, buffers pH swings, and slowly releases micronutrients.

salinity_sodicity.name: Electrical Conductivity & Sodicity (EC & ESP)
salinity_sodicity.definition: EC measures total dissolved salts in soil water, while Exchangeable Sodium Percentage (ESP) measures sodium saturation.
salinity_sodicity.significance: High salinity induces physiological drought in crop roots; high sodicity causes structural clay dispersion and crusting.
